summary: This program prints a 10 by 10 multiplication table using one loop inside another. The outer loop picks a row, the inner loop prints every product in that row, and each number is padded so the columns line up.

lines.text: The outer loop walks through the rows, giving i the values 1 through 10; range stops just before its second argument, so 11 is needed to include 10.
For every single value of i, this inner loop runs all the way from 1 to 10, which is what produces 100 products in total.
The f-string format :3 pads each product to three characters wide so the columns stay aligned, and end=' ' replaces the usual newline with a space so the row keeps building on one line.
This empty print belongs to the outer loop, so after each finished row it emits the newline that end=' ' suppressed, moving on to the next row.
